transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

Hi, yeah, thanks. Well, what brings me in is... I guess it's what happens after my late shifts at the plant. They moved me to the swing shift a few months back, and let me tell you, it completely throws off your whole rhythm. The traffic is better on the way home, at least, but... anyway, after I clock out, I'll stop for takeout. There's this place right off the highway, and I'll end up ordering two burgers, fries, a shake, and I just eat it all. 

But then I get home, and... well, I have this old spare fridge out in the garage. I originally put it out there because my wife couldn't stand the smell of the bait I use for fishing down at the lake, but we keep extra food in it now. And I'll just stand out there and clean out whatever leftovers we have in it. It's like I'm having a whole second supper, right there in the garage next to my tools. I just... I don't know why I keep doing it.
Do you ever feel like you can't control how much you're eating during these late meals, like you just can't stop once you start?

Yeah, that's exactly it. Once I start, it feels like a switch is flipped, you know? Even while I’m standing there telling myself, 'Roy, shut the bag and go inside,' my hands just keep reaching for more. It's usually those giant bags of chips my wife gets at Costco. Have you ever tried going to Costco on a Saturday? It is an absolute madhouse. I keep telling her we should go on a Tuesday morning, but with my new swing shift, our schedules are completely out of whack now. 

She likes to buy in bulk to save money, which makes sense, especially with the price of everything these days. Gas alone is just killing us. I drive an older F-150 and it just drinks gas on the highway. I’ve been meaning to check the spark plugs on it, actually, maybe this weekend if I have the energy. I keep my good socket wrench set right next to that spare fridge out in the garage, so I'll see it and remind myself. But... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, the food. Yeah, I just can't seem to make myself stop once I get going out there.
Does this eating behavior in the garage ever bother you, or cause any problems with your daily life, like with your family, work, or how you feel about yourself?

Well, I mean... I still get to work on time, mostly. The plant is pretty strict about clocking in. And my wife and I still go to church on Sundays. Our pastor, Reverend Miller, he just had his knee replaced. Poor guy was hobbling around for months before he finally got the surgery. They say they use some kind of titanium joint now, which is incredible when you think about the engineering behind it. I actually took some metallurgy classes back when I tried community college for a bit, before I started at the plant. It's fascinating stuff, how they treat the metal.

But... yeah, the eating. It bothers me, for sure. I guess I've been pulling away a bit at home. It just takes so much energy, you know? Like, making sure I throw away the fast food wrappers in the outside bin before I pull into the garage so my wife doesn't see them. And then I have to come up with some excuse for why I'm not hungry for the dinner she left in the main fridge for me. She makes this great meatloaf, but I just can't eat it after I've already stuffed myself. So I end up kind of hiding out, trying to cover my tracks. It just makes me feel... lousy.
Has this eating behavior ever caused you to avoid spending time with your family, affected your performance at work, or made you feel bad about yourself afterward?

Yeah, I guess it really does make me feel bad about myself. Afterward, I just feel... ashamed, you know? And honestly, kind of disgusted with myself. I've always been a guy who takes pride in being disciplined. I mean, I've been at the plant for twenty-two years, never missed a shift unless I was dead on my feet. My supervisor, Gary, he always says, "Roy, you're the most dependable guy on the line." Gary's retiring next year, actually. Going to move down to Florida, buy a boat. I keep telling him the humidity down there is going to ruin his joints, but he won't listen. He’s got his heart set on catching tarpon. I’ve always preferred bass fishing myself, right here at the local lake. The water's a bit murky this time of year because of the algae bloom, but if you use a topwater lure right at dawn... 

Wait, sorry. What was I... right. The eating. Yeah, it just goes against everything I think I am. I’m dependable, I’m disciplined, but then I’m out there in the garage sneaking around like a teenager trying to hide a pack of cigarettes. It just makes me feel like I’m really letting myself down, you know? It’s hard to look in the mirror after.
After you eat like that in the garage, do you ever make yourself sick, fast, or exercise a lot to try to control your weight or get rid of the calories?

No, no, I don't do anything like that. I could never make myself throw up, I just hate being sick. And as for exercising... well, I used to try walking on this old treadmill we have down in the basement, but it basically just turned into a very expensive clothes hanger. My wife bought it off Craigslist a couple of years ago from this couple moving out to Arizona. They had a beautiful house, mid-century modern, you know? Hardwood floors throughout the whole place. I've always wanted to put hardwood in our living room, but the cost of lumber right now is just highway robbery. I went to Home Depot last week just to price out some basic pine boards for a workbench project I've been meaning to start, and I almost had a heart attack right there in the aisle. The kid working in the lumber department said it's all because of supply chain issues, but honestly, I think they just know people are going to pay it anyway. You can't even build a simple birdhouse these days without taking out a second mortgage. 

But... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, the treadmill. Yeah, no, I don't go working out for hours or starving myself the next day or anything like that. I just wake up feeling heavy and guilty, eat my regular breakfast, and head into the plant.
How often do you find yourself eating a large amount of food in one sitting, like what you described happening in the garage?

Well, let's see... for the past few months, it's been pretty regular. There's usually at least one night a week where I end up doing it, and honestly, it's often two or three nights. It usually happens after a late shift or if I've had a really rough day on the line. 

You know, the line has been brutal lately. They've got us running this new batch of parts for a contract they just picked up, and the machinery keeps jamming. The maintenance guys are pulling their hair out trying to figure it out. One of them, Dave, he's a good guy, but he's getting up there in years. He was telling me in the breakroom that his daughter just had twins. Boy and a girl. They live out in Oregon, so he's trying to save up some vacation time to go see them. I told him he better go during the summer, because the rain out there in the winter is just miserable. My wife and I went to Portland about ten years ago for a cousin's wedding, and it rained the entire five days we were there. Beautiful trees, though. Those Douglas firs are something else. 

But, uh, yeah... so it's usually one to three times a week, mostly when I'm just beat from work and pull into the garage.
